This looks like early 2019. The fed funds rate at 2.41% fits the period after the December 2018 hike. The 3-month equity return of +14.4% with a 6-month return of -1.6% points to a rebound from the December 2018 low, which puts the snapshot at the end of March 2019.

Other figures fit as well. The 10-year yield was about 2.39% at the end of March 2019, and the 2-year was about 2.23%. The VIX was about 13.7–14.4. Unemployment was 3.8% and headline CPI was 1.5%. The dollar was up strongly year over year.

Treasuries were up 2.7% in the month, which also matches March 2019, when yields fell sharply.
